data.title: Gold, silver crash: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller fall up to 5%; bullion to decline further? What experts say
data.description:
Jewellery stocks witnessed heavy selling pressure on Friday, November 20, as a sharp correction in domestic and international gold and silver prices weighed on sentiment. Shares of jewellery companies, including Kalyan Jewellers, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri (TBZ), PC Jeweller, Titan Company and Thangamayil Jewellery, declined up to 5 percent, extending their losses for a third consecutive session.

The selloff came as gold prices further declined on Friday and were headed for their worst week in eight months, while silver extended its slid, losing around 14 percent during the week. The sharp correction in precious metals raised concerns over near-term sentiment in jewellery stocks, even as several of them have delivered strong returns so far in 2026.

Titan Company emerged as the top loser on the Nifty 50 index, falling 3.8 percent to an intraday low of Rs 4,524 apiece, compared with its previous close of Rs 4,700.

Kalyan Jewellers was the top loser on the Nifty 500 index, plunging 5.17 percent to an intra-day low of Rs 617. PC Jewellers shares fell 4.5 percent to hit an intra-day low of Rs 13.85, against its previous close of Rs 14.51.

Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri (TBZ) shares opened at Rs 573 and declined 4.7 percent to an intra-day low of Rs 545.95 while Thangamayil Jewellery shares opened at Rs 3,939.70 and dropped 2 percent to touch an intra-day low of Rs 3,860.10.

The latest declines came despite strong year-to-date gains across jewellery stocks. Titan has risen 13 percent so far in 2026, while Kalyan Jewellers has gained over 28 percent. PC Jeweller has rallied 50 percent so far this year, while Thangamayil Jewellery has advanced 19 percent and TBZ has rallied the most, rising 231 percent year-to-date.

The broader markets, however, remain in positive territory. At around 12.18 pm, the Sensex was up 495 points, or 0.6 percent, at 823,516.77, while the Nifty was trading 8.6 points or 0.03 percent higher at 25,522.90.

Gold, silver prices extend losses

International gold prices continued to decline on Friday, with spot gold dropping 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 8.9% for the week, marking its sharpest weekly fall since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery declined 3.6% to $3,551.90, as per Reuters report.

Silver also extended its decline, falling 2.3 percent to $41.98 per ounce after plunging nearly 5 percent in the previous session. The metal has lost around 14 percent during the week.

"There seems to be a bit of forced liquidation going on across the market in general, with expectations of imminent US rate hikes and inflation that could be persistent, leading to high yields and a higher US dollar as a result, pressuring gold," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, as quoted by Reuters.

In the domestic market, the precious metals declined. On MCX, the Multi Commodity Exchange of India Limited (MCX), which is India's largest commodity derivatives exchange, gold fell nearly 4% to Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 gram while silver plunged nearly 6%, slumping to Rs 1.48 lakh per kg at the opening of the day's trade.

Gold, silver prices fall: Bullion to decline further? What experts say

Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities, said, “Gold remains under significant pressure after a sharp correction of more than Rs 6,000 over the last two sessions. COMEX Gold is facing resistance below $3,750, while MCX prices have slipped below Rs 1,29,300, reflecting continued selling pressure. The next major support is seen near Rs 1,25,000, while Rs 1,35,000 is likely to act as immediate resistance.”

“Going ahead, the US Federal Reserve's December policy meeting will remain the key trigger, with dollar strength, inflation expectations and the Fed's policy guidance likely to determine the next directional move. Overall sentiment remains weak, and volatility is expected to stay elevated,” Trivedi noted.

Kaveri More, Commodity Technical Analyst at Choice Broking, said gold prices continue to witness aggressive selling, declining around 3.5% during Friday’s session amid a stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields.

"COMEX gold is hovering near $3,538 per ounce, while MCX gold is trading around Rs 122,700, with further downside potential towards Rs 120,000," More said.

More believes the correction has been driven by hawkish Federal Reserve commentary, which has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy, while the unwinding of AI-related investments has triggered liquidity-driven selling in precious metals as investors raise cash. Despite the sharp decline, lower domestic gold prices are reviving wedding jewellery demand ahead of the festive season. However, budget-conscious consumers remain cautious, while jewellers prefer price stability to protect inventory margins, she added.

"Overall, the near-term trend remains bearish, with the dollar and US bond yields likely to remain key drivers. Silver prices have also witnessed significant selling pressure, with COMEX silver hovering around $41.65 per ounce and MCX silver trading below ₹150,000. The Gold/Silver ratio has climbed to a 14-month high of 85.5:1, highlighting silver’s relatively sharper weakness compared with gold. The broader precious-metals correction, driven by a stronger dollar, rising bond yields and liquidity-driven selling, continues to weigh on sentiment. The near-term outlook remains weak, and traders should watch for signs of price stabilisation before anticipating a sustained recovery," she added.

Why gold and silver prices are falling?

The selloff has been driven by expectations of further US interest-rate hikes as the Federal Reserve maintains a hawkish stance amid persistent inflationary pressures. Higher interest rates and bond yields typically weigh on gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.

Bullion has also faced selling pressure amid a rout in technology and AI-related stocks, prompting some investors to liquidate gold holdings to cover losses elsewhere.

Earlier on Thursday, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets see a 96.8% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 3.2%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

data.title: China's yttrium exports to US hit seven-month high
data.description:
China sent a sizeable amount of yttrium oxide, a rare earth used in aerospace, to the US in October, customs data showed on Friday.

China produces the vast majority of heavy rare earths such as yttrium, but exports have been restrained since it introduced export controls on several of them in April 2025.

  • China sent 38.5 metric tons of yttrium oxide to the US in October, the most since March, when it shipped 60 tons

  • October's volume was about 8.5 tons above the monthly average in the 12 months before the controls were introduced, and only the second month since the controls that shipments have topped that average

  • Shipments to the US have been erratic since the controls, with none recorded in nine of the 19 months from April 2025

  • China is the world's main source of yttrium, used in specialty alloys employed in engines as well as coatings to shield against high temperatures

  • Yttrium exports to Japan, once one of the largest buyers of Chinese rare earths and strategic metals, stayed low at 8 tons in October

  • Shipments to Japan have been sharply lower this year, after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan sparked a row with Beijing in November 2025

  • Exports to the US and Japan of other controlled rare earths like dysprosium and terbium oxides, used in powerful rare earth magnets, were at zero in October

  • US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, followed by a three-way meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

  • US officials have frequently complained about difficulties that US companies say they are experiencing in receiving sufficient quantities of rare earths from China

data.title: Japan futures log worst week since June on tepid Tokyo equities, tyre demand
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Japanese rubber futures were little changed on Friday and logged their biggest weekly loss since late June, pressured by a selloff in Asian equities and soft tyre demand.

  • The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery , was down 0.5 yen, or 0.12%, at 423.3 yen ($2.66) per kg

  • The contract lost 4.28% this week

  • The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery fell 100 yuan, or 0.53%, to 18,625 yuan ($2,791.43) per metric ton

  • The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) rose 295 yuan, or 1.93%, to 15,560 yuan per metric ton

  • Recent weak macroeconomic sentiment coupled with sluggish downstream demand has led to a renewed bearish market sentiment, analysts from Gelin Dahua Futures said in a note

  • Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5.06% to close at a seven-month low on Friday, posting a 7.7% weekly drop, as technology shares tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI trade

  • Capacity utilisation at sampled Chinese semi-steel and all-steel tyre makers was 62.05% and 58.72% in the week ended November 19, down 7.31 and 3.32 percentage points respectively from a year earlier, data from commodity information provider Longzhong Information showed

  • The domestic retail market for passenger cars in November will remain sluggish, with an estimated 1.63 million units sold for the month, down 1.1% from the previous month, said the China Passenger Car Association

  • Raw materials entered a high production phase in top producer Thailand, with rubber tapping operations improving in the northeast region, said analysts from GF Futures in a note

  • The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 238.5 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.7% as of 0705 GMT

($1 = 159.0900 yen)

data.title: Consumer confidence sparks as festive shopping season gets underway
data.description:
The latest consumer confidence index from GfK, part of the Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions , came in at -22, up two points on October’s sharp slide to -24.

Respondents were less confident about their personal finances in the coming year, with the measure falling two points to -5. But despite that they were more upbeat about the strength of the economy over the same period - with the measure up four points at -32 - while the major purchase index was five points stronger at -17.

The savings index, which is not included in the overall score, shed one point to 27.

Neil Bellamy, consumer insights director at GfK, said the small but "welcome" headline increase concealed larger movements in specific groups. Confidence among younger consumers spiked 11 points, and by six points across households that earn £50,000 or more.

"The main improvement within our five sub-measures came from the major purchase index," he said. "That should reassure manufacturers and retailers ahead of the crucial Black Friday and Christmas trading period that there are still people out there willing to spend."

However, Bellamy warned: "Consumers were already grappling with persistent inflationary pressures, and higher interest rates are likely to have placed additional strain on household budgets.

"While consumers appear willing to support seasonal spending, the continued deterioration in personal financial sentiment suggests that confidence remains fragile and vulnerable to further economic pressures in the months ahead."

The Bank of England had left interest rates on hold for most of the year, at a historically high 3.75%, but earlier this month voted to lift the cost of borrowing to 4% in the face of mounting inflationary pressures. The consumer price index currently stands at 3.6%.

Most analysts expect another hike in December, with some predicting Bank Rate could reach 5% by the middle of next year.

data.title: Gints Ozoliņš steps down as Head of Technology at INDEXO Group, with Krišjānis Bērzs and Mareks Rudovičs taking over his responsibilities
data.description:
Effective 20 November 2026, Gints Ozoliņš will step down as Head of Technology at the INDEXO financial services group and will also leave his positions as a member of the Management Board of AS INDEXO Banka and AS INDEXO Atklātais Pensiju Fonds. Going forward, the technological development of INDEXO Group will be jointly led by Mareks Rudovičs and Krišjānis Bērzs, who joined the Group in October this year.

Gints Ozoliņš has been part of the INDEXO team since the early stages of the establishment of INDEXO Bank, making a significant contribution to building the Bank’s technology infrastructure, developing its information systems and launching the Bank’s operations.

“I would like to thank Gints for his contribution to the establishment and development of INDEXO Bank. Gints has been with us since the Bank’s first day, helping to build it and contributing to one of the most ambitious projects in Latvia’s financial sector, the establishment of a new locally owned bank. We are grateful for everything we have accomplished together and wish Gints every success in his future professional endeavours. At the same time, INDEXO Group continues to grow and develop, attracting new talent and expertise. The addition of Mareks Rudovičs and Krišjānis Bērzs to our management team will strengthen our technology development capabilities and enable us to continue working on new, innovative financial services,” says Valdis Siksnis, co-founder of INDEXO Group and Chairman of the Management Board of INDEXO Bank.

Mareks Rudovičs and Krišjānis Bērzs are co-founders of the Latvian technology company Roibox and have extensive experience in IT and technology management, data analytics, financial technology (FinTech), business process automation and the development of artificial intelligence solutions. Roibox, which specialises in data-driven digital marketing and business optimisation solutions, was acquired in 2026 by Jakala, an international Italian technology and marketing company.

Krišjānis Bērzs specialises in data architecture, data management and business intelligence solutions, including the management of IT infrastructure and technology solution development. Mareks Rudovičs’ professional experience, in turn, covers data analytics, credit risk modelling and the automation of data-driven business processes. In recent years, both have also focused particularly on the development and implementation of artificial intelligence solutions and autonomous workflows.

Both new technology leaders joined INDEXO Group in October 2026 and will jointly be responsible for the Group’s technological development going forward, supporting the continued growth of INDEXO Banka and other Group companies.

Companies closely associated with Mareks Rudovičs and Krišjānis Bērzs each acquired 160,000 new INDEXO shares in the private placement of 10 November 2026 at a price of EUR 2.50 per share.

About the INDEXO financial services group

INDEXO is a financial services group comprising the pension management companies IPAS INDEXO, INDEXO Atklātais Pensiju Fonds AS and INDEXO Asset Management IPAS, as well as AS INDEXO Banka (INDEXO Bank) and DelfinGroup AS.

The Group's pension companies manage EUR 1.75 billion for 162.2 thousand customer accounts in Latvia. INDEXO Bank, a bank licensed by the European Central Bank, serves 69.8 thousand customers with deposits of EUR 159.9 million and a net loan portfolio of EUR 134.0 million. Data as of 30 September 2026. The Group reached profitability in the first quarter of this year.

data.title: Iron ore rises on restocking hopes, but post weekly loss
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Iron ore futures rose on Friday on hopes of year-end restocking by steel mills, though the contracts posted a weekly loss after breaking through previous lows earlier in the week amid weak demand and high port stocks.

The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) traded 0.62% higher at 652.5 yuan ($97.79) a metric ton.

The contract lost 2.09% this week.

The benchmark December iron ore <SZZFZ6> on the Singapore Exchange was 0.17% higher at $88.5 a ton, falling 2.16% this week.

Steel mills' raw material costs have fallen with iron ore prices, and year-end restocking could provide some short-term support, though low profits mean purchases are likely to be cautious, analysts from broker Minmetals Futures said in a note.

Imported sintering powder inventories at 114 steel mills rose 1.29 million tons to 27.75 million tons this week, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports rose 0.74% from the previous week to 157.36 million tons, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.

Futures broke through previous lows on November 16 and fell as low as 638.5 yuan a ton on November 18, as expectations of tighter US Federal Reserve policy sapped risk appetite, the Minmetals analysts said.

Elsewhere, executives at iron ore majors BHP and Rio Tinto are due to meet with China's premier and business leaders in Beijing on Friday, amid increasingly fraught negotiations between Australia's top miners and China's state iron ore buyer, China Mineral Resources Group.

Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE climbed, with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1) up 2.61% and 3.12%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar rose 0.54% and hot-rolled coil gained 0.19%, while stainless steel fell 1.19%.

($1 = 6.6722 Chinese yuan)

data.title: OakNorth Secures U.S. Federal Reserve Clearance to Buy Community Unity Bank
data.description:
(07:02 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Receives Federal Reserve Approval to Buy Community Unity Bank
(07:02 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Receives Office of the Comptroller of the Currency Approval to Buy Community Unity Bank
(07:03 GMT) *OakNorth Bank to Restructure Group Entities to Meet Federal Reserve Requirements
(07:03 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Expects Transaction to Complete by End of 2026
(07:21 GMT) OakNorth Secures U.S. Federal Reserve Clearance to Buy Community Unity Bank

By Michael Hennessey

British lender OakNorth Bank has received approval from the U.S. Federal Reserve to buy Michigan-based Community Unity Bank.

The U.K. digital bank said its acquisition of Community Unity Bank has been approved by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. The all-stock deal was first announced in March 2025.

To meet the Federal Reserve's requirements, OakNorth said it will restructure its entities. On completion, Community Unity Bank will become a member of the group.

OakNorth was set up in 2015 and specializes in offering debt finance to mid-market businesses that are seeking to scale.

The Community Unity Bank is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation-insured bank in Oakland County, Michigan, which offers a full range of banking products and services.

London-based fintech OakNorth expects the transaction and restructuring to complete by the end of the year.

Write to Michael Hennessey at michael.hennessey@wsj.com
